label: Magic superstition
summary: A short misfortune phrase: a poor harvest, bad weather or sick animals.
details: Works on a character. The three entries have no condition in vanilla. The game marks it as usable for a random pick. Going by the key name, these are things people might blame on magic.

label: Magic user
summary: The word for someone who uses magic: witch for a female character, sorcerer for anyone else.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks by whether the character is female.

label: Tournament kind
summary: A word for a martial contest: jousting, wrestling or sparring.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla gives jousting to a character with a feudal government whose capital is in western Europe. Wrestling goes to one with a tribal government, a faith with the pagan hostility doctrine, or a capital in northern Europe. The condition for sparring was not read.

label: Mask or face
summary: The word mask for a disfigured character, the word face for anyone else.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla's board game texts use it for the spot where a character's expression shows.

label: Behind or across
summary: The word behind for a disfigured character, the word across for anyone else, to go before mask or face.
details: Works on a character. A vanilla comment gives the idea: a frown twisting behind the mask rather than across the face.

label: Behind or in
summary: The word behind for a disfigured character, the word in for anyone else, to go before mask or face.
details: Works on a character. A vanilla comment gives the idea: a vein bulging behind the mask rather than in the face.

label: Conversation subject
summary: A topic two characters might talk about, such as new strategies, ancient military campaigns or the lords and ladies of the realm.
details: Works on a character and the saved scope second, the other person in the talk. It has 14 entries covering martial, diplomacy, charm, learning, stewardship and intrigue topics, plus fighting techniques and the weather. The first entry (new strategies) needs both people to have martial education or a martial lifestyle; the other conditions were not read. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Conversation subject (alone)
summary: A topic of conversation drawn from the same 14 topics as the plain conversation subject, but fitted to the character alone.
details: Works on a character, and can be picked at random. The entry list is the same as the plain version. In vanilla the first entry (new strategies) checks only this character for martial education or a martial lifestyle, not a second person.

label: Matriarch or patriarch
summary: The word matriarch for a female character, patriarch for anyone else.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks only by whether the character is female.

label: Mistress or master
summary: The word mistress for a female character, master for a male one.
details: Works on a character.

label: Battle month
summary: The name of a month, January to December.
details: Works on a province. Vanilla reads the number from the province's variable battle_poi_date_month (1 to 12). The entry names say it belongs to a battle point of interest, a marked battle site.

label: Monument description
summary: A short description of what kind of monument a province holds, such as a beautiful natural wonder, an impressive mine or a majestic fortress.
details: Works on a province, which it saves as scope location while choosing. It has 15 entries: natural wonders, mines, buildings and grand structures, up to a legendary hallmark. Vanilla ties the natural wonder entries to a province whose travel point of interest is a natural feature, and some building entries to a building with the flag travel_point_of_interest_economic. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Monument sighting line
summary: A first-person sentence about first seeing a monument from far off, such as the silhouette breaking the horizon.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla saves the character's current location as scope location, and each of the three sentences inserts the monument description of that location. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Mother or father
summary: The word mother for a female character, father for anyone else.
details: Works on a character.

label: Mother's or father's
summary: The possessive mother's for a female character, father's for anyone else.
details: Works on a character.

label: Knightly
summary: The adjective for a mounted warrior, knightly.
details: Works on a character. Its only entry has no condition in vanilla (a comment there mentions Faris for Muslims). The entry takes its text from another game text whose name speaks of the player's culture, in lowercase and without a tooltip; that text is not shown in the input.

label: Knight
summary: The word for a mounted warrior, knight.
details: Works on a character. Its only entry has no condition in vanilla. The entry takes its text from another game text whose name speaks of the player's culture, in lowercase and without a tooltip; that text is not shown in the input.

label: Knights
summary: The plural word for mounted warriors, knights.
details: Works on a character. Its only entry has no condition in vanilla (a comment there mentions Faris for Muslims). The entry takes its text from another game text whose name speaks of the player's culture, in lowercase and without a tooltip; that text is not shown in the input.

label: Muhammad's sword
summary: The name and a short note on one of nine swords the game attributes to Muhammad.
details: Works on a character. Each entry key is artifact_wall_sword_muhammad_ followed by the sword's name, for example Al-'Adb or Al-Battar, and its text adds a short note on where the sword came from. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Murder memory ending
summary: The closing phrase of a memory about a murder, such as but now I have my revenge or but you reap what you sow.
details: Works on a character. There are four endings: revenge, justice, sleeping easier and reaping what you sow. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Musical performer
summary: The word for a musical performer. Its only entry is troubadour.
details: Works on a character. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Performer's
summary: The possessive of the musical performer word: troubadour's.
details: Works on a character. Its only entry is troubadour's.

label: Introduce as mine
summary: Introduces a character as seen by the speaker, in the form my ... or X, the ... of Y.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla uses the plain no-comma introduction when the character has a relation to the saved scope second or holds a primary title, and otherwise the same introduction with a comma added.

label: Introduce as mine (no comma)
summary: Introduces a character from the speaker's point of view: my council title and first name, my relation and titled first name, or X, the relation of Y.
details: Works on a character. Entries cover the character's council title, their relation to the speaker, and being the spouse, father, mother, councillor or knight of someone. A fallback entry applies when none fits. Which entry wins depends on conditions the input does not show.

label: Introduce as mine (possessive)
summary: The same introduction of a character as the plain version, with and without a trailing comma.
details: Works on a character. Its two entries call the same no-comma introduction as the plain version, so in the input it shows no difference from it.

label: Priest title
summary: The word for a priest in the faith of the character, in a male, female or neutral form.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla chooses by the gender of the character's court chaplain councillor. The text is the matching priest word of the character's faith.

label: Introduce by owner's name
summary: Introduces a character through someone else's name in the possessive, followed by the council title or relation, with or without a trailing comma.
details: Works on a character. Its two entries call the no-comma version; the second adds a comma.

label: Introduce by owner's name (no comma)
summary: Introduces a character through another character's possessive name: their name's, then the council title and first name, or the relation and titled first name.
details: Works on a character. It also has entries for being the spouse, father, mother, councillor or knight of someone, and a fallback. Which entry wins depends on conditions the input does not show.

label: Negative afterlife
summary: The name of the place or realm where the bad dead go, in the faith, such as hell or the underworld.
details: Works on a faith. It has 31 entries, for example among the Nsamanfo, hell, the underworld or Myalba, and ends in a fallback entry.

label: Negative greeting add-on
summary: An extra insulting line added to a greeting, such as May your years be short and miserable.
details: Works on a character. It has 24 entries: general insults, and ones aimed at Muslims, Christians, Norse, Byzantines, Jews, Zoroastrians and Hindus. The game marks it as usable for a random pick. Note the key's spelling (Suppliment) is the game's own.

label: Nickname note
summary: A short sentence saying the character was known in life by their nickname, or nothing at all.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla gives Known in life as followed by the nickname when the character has any nickname, and the empty blank_line entry when not. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Night god name
summary: A name for the night god of a faith, in a variant the key calls cel.
details: Works on a faith. It has 42 entries and the input shows no text for them. Vanilla picks the entry by the faith's religion (for example a Christianity entry first). What cel stands for is not documented. The manicheanism entry appears twice in the game's list. The meaning rests on the key and entry names.

label: Nun or monk
summary: The word for a devotee of the character's faith, in a female, male or neutral form.
details: Works on a character. Each entry reads the matching devotee word from the character's faith. The neutral one is the fallback.

label: Thing to climb
summary: An object that could be climbed: a sand dune, a boulder or a tree.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla gives a sand dune when the character is in desert terrain, a boulder in plains, mountains, desert mountains, drylands or steppe, and a tree otherwise.

label: Objectified body feature
summary: A body feature of the character that a remark might single out, such as amorous lips, ample curves or graceful feet.
details: Works on a character. It has nine entries. Amorous lips has no condition; ample bosom, curves, generous rear and delicate wrists need a female character, and shapely legs a male one. Ankles and shapely legs also need the character not to be one-legged. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Council offer speech
summary: The words of a liege offering a council position, in four tones: to a liked subject, grudgingly, to a powerful vassal, or as a last resort.
details: Works on the liege, with the saved scope second as the person offered the job. Vanilla picks liked when the liege's opinion of that person is 30 or more, disliked when it is below -30, powerful when that person is a powerful vassal of the liege, and fallback otherwise. The texts name the position and the offering ruler's primary title. The stored texts show literal backslash-n marks where line breaks are meant.

label: Lowly servant type
summary: A lowly household servant job, such as stable boy, page, scullery maid, chandler or servant.
details: Works on a character, and can be picked at random. It has 11 entries. Vanilla ties several entries to the character being female (stable boy, page, chandler) or male (scullery maid, launderer), and some also to the character's government type; the last entry, servant, has a lower weight (0.3). The key's word opposite-gendered is not otherwise explained.

label: Conquest ordinal ending
summary: The ending st, nd or rd after a number kept on a title, the count of grand campaign projects.
details: Works on a title. The number comes from the title's variable num_of_grand_campaign_projects. Entries exist for st, nd, rd, zero and a fallback; the input shows no text for the zero entry and does not show the fallback's.

label: Battle day ordinal
summary: The day number of a battle site's date followed by its ordinal ending: 1st, 2nd, 3rd, or th for other days.
details: Works on a province. The number comes from the province's variable battle_poi_date_day.

label: Outdoor hiding place
summary: A place to hide outdoors: trees or rocks.
details: Works on a character. Neither entry has a condition in vanilla, whose comment calls it something you find in nature or by the road.

label: Polish god word (form 1)
summary: One of five Polish word forms for god or gods, chosen by the faith of the character's house head.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla gives Boze when the house head's religion is Christianity, Islam or Judaism, Doskonali for Buddhism, Niebiosa for dualism or Zoroastrianism, and Bogowie for any other. Inne is the fallback entry. The input shows no texts for the entries. Its sibling PL_2_GetAppropriateGodname holds a second set of forms.

label: Polish god word (form 2)
summary: A second set of five Polish word forms for god or gods, chosen by the faith of the character's house head.
details: Works on a character. Same conditions as the first form key: Boga for Christianity, Islam or Judaism, Doskonalych for Buddhism, Niebiosa2 for dualism or Zoroastrianism, Bogow for any other, and Inne2 as fallback. The input shows no texts for the entries.

label: Activity string bypass
summary: A custom text for an activity from the game's Polish text files; the game documents nothing more.
details: Works on an activity. It has one entry, pl_activity_string_bypass, used as the fallback; the input shows no text for it. What the text does is not documented.

label: Polish cie
summary: The Polish word form cie, or an empty form for characters whose house head follows Christianity, Islam or Judaism.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla gives CustomLoc_PL_Brak when the house head's religion is Christianity, Islam or Judaism. The CustomLoc_PL_Cie entry is the fallback, so it applies to every other house head. The input shows no texts; that Brak is empty is a guess from the Polish word for none.

label: Female animal
summary: The word for a female hunted animal: doe, roe deer, hind, wolf, vixen, jill, cow, elk, boar or a fallback.
details: Vanilla defines it for any scope. It picks by the variable animal_type (stag gives doe, hart gives hind, and so on). Only doe and hind show their English text in the input. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Male animal
summary: The word for a male hunted animal: stag, roe deer, dog, wolf, jack, bull, boar or a fallback.
details: Vanilla defines it for any scope, and picks by the variable animal_type. The stag entry shows the text buck; the Polish entries show no text in the input. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Diarch title
summary: The title word for a character's diarch: vizier, regent, or a fallback.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla gives the vizier entry for the vizierate diarchy type, the regent entry for a regency or temporary regency, and the fallback for any other. The input shows no texts for the entries.

label: Diarchy type name
summary: The name of the character's diarchy kind: vizierate, temporary regency, regency (the ent_regency entry), or a fallback.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks by the diarchy type: vizierate, temporary_regency or regency, with the fallback for any other. The input shows no texts for the entries; what ent stands for is not explained.

label: Ruler word by government
summary: The word for a ruler in the genitive case, chosen by the character's government: landless adventurer, feudal, clan, tribal, theocracy, republic, or a fallback.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks the entry by the government type. The input shows no texts for the entries. The genitive is a Polish grammar case.

label: Polish go / ja
summary: The male Polish word form (go) for a male character, the female form (ja) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks by whether the character is female. The input shows no texts; the go and ja words come from the key name.

label: Polish go / jej
summary: The male Polish word form (go) for a male character, the female form (jej) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks by whether the character is female. The input shows no texts; the words come from the key name.

label: Polish jego / ja
summary: The male Polish word form (jego) for a male character, the female form (ja) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks by whether the character is female. The input shows no texts; the words come from the key name.

label: Polish jego / jej
summary: The male Polish word form (jego, his) for a male character, the female form (jej, her) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks by whether the character is female. The input shows no texts; the words come from the key name.

label: Polish his/her/my (moi)
summary: The Polish moi form of my, his or her: my for the player's own character, otherwise by the character's gender.
details: Works on a character. It has three entries. Vanilla gives the _my entry when the character is the local player, the _male entry when the character is not female, and the _female entry when she is. The input shows no texts.

label: Polish his/her/my (moich)
summary: The Polish moich form of my, his or her: my for the player's own character, otherwise by the character's gender.
details: Works on a character. It has three entries: _my when the character is the local player, otherwise _male or _female by gender. The input shows no texts.

label: Polish his/her/my (moim)
summary: The Polish moim form of my, his or her: my for the player's own character, otherwise by the character's gender.
details: Works on a character. It has three entries: _my when the character is the local player, otherwise _male or _female by gender. The input shows no texts.

label: Polish his/her/my (moimi)
summary: The Polish moimi form of my, his or her: my for the player's own character, otherwise by the character's gender.
details: Works on a character. It has three entries: _my when the character is the local player, otherwise _male or _female by gender. The input shows no texts.

label: Polish his/her/my (moj)
summary: The Polish moj form of my, his or her: my for the player's own character, otherwise by the character's gender.
details: Works on a character. It has three entries: _my when the character is the local player, otherwise _male or _female by gender. The input shows no texts.

label: Polish his/her/my (moje)
summary: The Polish moje form of my, his or her: my for the player's own character, otherwise by the character's gender.
details: Works on a character. It has three entries: _my when the character is the local player, otherwise _male or _female by gender. The input shows no texts.

label: Polish his/her/my (mojego)
summary: The Polish mojego form of my, his or her: my for the player's own character, otherwise by the character's gender.
details: Works on a character. It has three entries: _my when the character is the local player, otherwise _male or _female by gender. The input shows no texts.

label: Polish his/her/my (mojemu)
summary: The Polish mojemu form of my, his or her: my for the player's own character, otherwise by the character's gender.
details: Works on a character. It has three entries: _my when the character is the local player, otherwise _male or _female by gender. The input shows no texts.

label: Polish jemu / jej
summary: The male Polish word form (jemu) for a male character, the female form (jej) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. The condition was read for the sibling keys in the same file (is the character female); the input shows no texts.

label: Polish mu / jej
summary: The male Polish word form (mu) for a male character, the female form (jej) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. The condition was read for the sibling keys in the same file (is the character female); the input shows no texts.

label: Polish nephew
summary: Chooses between two nephew words: a nephew through a brother or through a sister.
details: Works on a character, with the saved scope second as the uncle or aunt. Vanilla gives the brother entry when the character's father is a sibling of the second character, and otherwise the sister entry (which also tests the mother). The input shows no texts.

label: Polish niece
summary: Chooses between two niece words: a niece through a brother or through a sister.
details: Works on a character, with the saved scope second as the uncle or aunt. Vanilla gives the brother entry when the character's father is a sibling of the second character, and otherwise the sister entry (which also tests the mother). The input shows no texts.

label: Polish niego / nia
summary: The male Polish word form (niego) for a male character, the female form (nia) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. The condition was read for the sibling keys in the same file (is the character female); the input shows no texts.

label: Polish niego / niej
summary: The male Polish word form (niego) for a male character, the female form (niej) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. The condition was read for the sibling keys in the same file (is the character female); the input shows no texts.

label: Polish niemu / niej
summary: The male Polish word form (niemu) for a male character, the female form (niej) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. The condition was read for the sibling keys in the same file (is the character female); the input shows no texts.

label: Polish nim / nia
summary: The male Polish word form (nim) for a male character, the female form (nia) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks by whether the character is female. The input shows no texts; the words come from the key name.

label: Polish nim / niej
summary: The male Polish word form (nim) for a male character, the female form (niej) for a female one.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks by whether the character is female. The input shows no texts; the words come from the key name.

label: Blessed ones term
summary: The group name for revered dead people, by religion: the blessed ones, the Awliya, the Divi, the Siddhas and so on.
details: Works on a character. It has ten entries: Christian, Islam, Hellenism, Jainism, Shinto, Confucianism, Buddhism, Taoism, Judaism and other. Only the first four texts are shown in the input.

label: Canonize verb
summary: The word for honouring someone as a saint, by religion: canonize, deify, honorifics, investiture or an other-religion word.
details: Works on a character. It has five entries: Christian, Hellenism, Confucianism, Taoism and other.

label: Consecrate or enshrine
summary: The verb consecrate for the Christian case, or enshrine for all other religions.
details: Works on a character. The entries are pam_consecrate_christian and pam_consecrate_others.

label: Fingerbone saint
summary: The name of a saint, such as Augustine of Hippo, Benedict of Nursia or Lawrence.
details: Works on a character. The list holds 16 entries, and saint_lawrence appears twice in it. Going by the key name, the saint is the one whose fingerbone relic is meant.

label: Saint noun
summary: The word for a canonized person, by religion, as a game concept: Saint, Waliyya or Wali, Diva or Divus, Siddha and so on.
details: Works on a character. Islam and Hellenism have separate female entries. Each text is a link to the game concept canonized.

label: Saint noun (generic)
summary: The word for a canonized person, by religion, without separate female forms: Saint, Wali, Divus, Siddha and so on.
details: Works on a character. It has ten entries, one per religion group, each a game-concept link.

label: Saint title
summary: The title given to a canonized person, by religion: Saint, Wali, Divus, Siddha and so on.
details: Works on a character. It has ten entries, one per religion group.

label: Saint title (plural)
summary: The plural of the saint title, by religion: Saints, Awliya, Divi, Siddhas and so on.
details: Works on a faith, not a character.

label: Rite acceptance chance
summary: A percentage in 10 per cent steps from 90% down to 0%, or the word unavailable when the sway is blocked.
details: Works on a character, who acts as the archbishop, with the saved scope second as the target. Vanilla shows unavailable when the archbishop cannot send the sway to the target (a comment says it would otherwise read as 0%), and otherwise the step whose acceptance check passes. It has 11 entries: blocked, then 90 down to 0. The blocked text uses a weak style, the 90, 80 and 70 shown use the game's positive style.

label: Venerated object title
summary: What is venerated, with a capital and an article: a Saint, a Wali, a Divus, a Siddha and so on.
details: Works on a character. It has ten entries: nine religions and an other-religion entry.

label: Venerated saint
summary: The phrase for a venerated person, by religion: a saint, a Wali or Waliyya, a Divus or Diva and so on.
details: Works on a character. It has 13 entries, with separate female forms for Islam, Hellenism and Judaism.

label: Venerated saint (generic)
summary: The phrase for a venerated person, by religion, without female forms: a saint, a Wali, a Divus, a Siddha.
details: Works on a character. It has ten entries, one per religion group.

label: Venerated saint title
summary: The phrase for a venerated person used where a title is meant, by religion: a saint, a Wali, a Divus and so on.
details: Works on a character. It has ten entries; only the last (other religion) uses its own title entry. It reuses the same entries as the generic version otherwise.

label: Pantheon term
summary: What a faith calls its divine powers, such as the Abosom, the powers, the gods, the samsara, a high god's name or the spirits.
details: Works on a faith. It has 15 entries and ends in a fallback. Vanilla picks the entry by the faith's religion; for example the Akom religion gets the Abosom and the Basque religion the powers.

label: Pantheon term is female
summary: A yes or no flag, pt_true or pt_false, for whether the pantheon term counts as female; the game documents nothing more.
details: Works on a faith. Vanilla gives pt_true for the Buddhism, dualism, paganism and West African orisha religions and pt_false for everything else. The input shows no text for either entry, so what the flag controls is not known beyond the key name.

label: Parent piety level
summary: The name of a piety level, from Sinner at level 0 up to level 8, such as Dutiful, Faithful or Devoted Servant.
details: Works on a character. It has nine entries, one per level. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Parent prestige level
summary: The name of a prestige level, from Disgraced at level 0 up to level 5, such as Established, Distinguished or Illustrious.
details: Works on a character. It has six entries, one per level. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Part aglow
summary: A phrase saying a body part seems aglow: eyes, eye, face or body.
details: Works on a character. The game marks it as usable for a random pick. Vanilla gives the plural eyes entry to a character who is neither blind nor one-eyed and the singular eye entry to a one-eyed one who is not blind.

label: Partner opinion word
summary: A word describing a partner, either a warm one for high opinion or a respectful one for low opinion.
details: Works on a character, with the saved scope second as the partner. Vanilla picks the warm word when the character's opinion of the partner is 50 or more, and the respectful word when it is below 50. Each entry passes the choice on to the high-opinion or low-opinion word list.

label: Warm partner word
summary: A warm word for a partner: darling, precious, sweet or lovely.
details: Works on a character. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Respectful partner word
summary: A respectful word for a partner: esteemed, imposing or respectable.
details: Works on a character. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Permanent injury word
summary: The name of a lasting injury: one-leggedness, one-eyedness, blindness, eunuchry, deformity or scarification.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks the entry by the character's trait: one-legged, one-eyed, blind, eunuch and further injury traits. Despite the key's word adjective, the texts are nouns.

label: Bible quote
summary: A Bible verse relevant to a personal tenet, shown in Latin, Greek or the default English.
details: Works on a character. It has 351 entries, three per verse (_latin, _greek, _default), the Latin and English ones shown as glossary tooltips. The Greek entries show no text in the input. Several verses appear twice in the list. The game marks it as usable for a random pick.

label: Brave test word
summary: The word brave when a trait flag says brave, otherwise bland.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla gives brave when the saved scope has_shared_trait holds the flag brave. The bland entry is the fallback and its own condition can never be true. It reads like a test entry for the personality word keys.

label: Negative trait word
summary: A word for the negative side of a trait the character has, for example cocky for arrogant, lewd for lustful, prudish for chaste.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks the entry by the trait the character has, starting with arrogant. It has 36 entries, one per personality trait, ending with a no-trait entry.

label: Positive trait word
summary: A positive word keyed to a trait the character has; the first entry gives confident for a humble character.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla picks by the trait the character has, and the entry named for the opposite trait: humble gives the entry named arrogant (confident). It has 36 entries, ending with a no-trait fallback. The list names compassionate twice and has no sadistic entry, unlike the shared-trait list.

label: Shared trait word (by flag)
summary: A positive word for a trait the two characters share, chosen by a flag; for example confident for arrogant or romantic for lustful.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla reads the saved scope has_shared_trait, which must hold a flag named like the trait (flag:arrogant gives confident). It has 36 entries; the last is the negative no-trait entry.

label: Trait word (by flag)
summary: A negative-side word for a trait, chosen by a flag; for example cocky for arrogant.
details: Works on a character. Vanilla reads the saved scope has_opposing_trait, which must hold a flag named like the trait (flag:arrogant gives cocky). It has 36 entries, ending with a no-trait fallback.

label: Trait word (by flag, inverted)
summary: A positive word for the opposite of a trait given by a flag; for example confident when the flag is humble.
details: Works on a character. A vanilla comment says it outputs a descriptor of the opposite trait of the flag held in the saved scope has_opposing_trait. Compassionate appears twice in its list and sadistic is missing.

label: Trait link (by flag, inverted)
summary: A link showing the name of the opposite trait of a flag, for example the arrogant trait's name when the flag is humble.
details: Works on a character. A vanilla comment says it is for use with the inverted word key, but in tooltips. Each entry looks up one trait and shows its name for the character. Compassionate appears twice in its list and sadistic is missing.
